Release updates

Starting with 0.9.0, MTL Explorer checks a small public JSON feed at https://mtl-explorer.com/releases/releases.json. The server performs the check; browsers only request the cached result from /mtl/api/info/updates.

On this page
  • User flow
  • Identities
  • Components and deployment releases
  • Network restrictions
  • Release publication
  • Isolated E2E preview
  • Publishing a component bundle

User flow

  • One notice introduces an available release. Dismiss keeps the Settings badge.
  • Desktop Settings and mobile More show the shared glowing dot. Expanded mobile Settings keeps the Update label.
  • View update or Settings → Updates opens versions, the summary, release notes, and update instructions.
  • Skip this version hides its notice and badge. The next release can notify again.
  • Reminder preferences belong to the browser, signed-in username, and installation.
  • The installation owner updates Docker Compose. Detection never installs or restarts anything.
  • After a detected installation change, one completion notice links to the notes.
  • A waiting browser service worker offers Reload or Later, including before login. Release offers remain signed-in only. Later keeps the navigation dot, a Reload label in expanded mobile Settings, and a reload action in Updates; it never interrupts work automatically.

Identities

Identity Example Purpose
Public release 0.9.0 Display, release notes, semantic version comparison
Immutable image build 1.520 Match the running Docker image to the public catalog
Image digest sha256:… Verify the exact published image before offering it
Git revision commit SHA Private build traceability and diagnostics

Images carry their immutable build identity; public versions are chosen when publishing and bound to verified builds in the release catalog. No public version is bundled in the application. Docker build tags keep their existing numbering; Git history does not decide release order. The public feed contains no private Git revision, tree, or build record.

About shows the image build and, when the cached catalog identifies the installed component combination, its deployment release. Before a feed is available, the semantic release remains unknown. Local frontend builds show their development package version. Retain published mappings so older installations remain identifiable.

The feed maps releases to immutable builds and has separate channel pointers. The same build promoted to a public release is already installed. An unregistered custom or older build reports unknown rather than guessing. Earlier versions do not acquire this checker retroactively: 0.9.0 is the first checking installation, and its first normal offer will be a later release. Preview screenshots use an isolated synthetic 0.8.1 → 0.9.0 mapping to illustrate the flow.

Components and deployment releases

One notice and badge cover self-managed MTL components. Updates lists the server, routing, location search, and maps with installed and target image builds. Provider-managed services are informational; disabled services are ignored. Unknown ownership or builds never imply an update or incompatibility. Unknown ownership stays visible on the component row but does not block the overall status or completion notice for tracked, self-managed components. An unknown build in a self-managed component still prevents claiming it is current.

The feed's optional components map describes a tested deployment combination. Each target contains buildId, image, and digest. Component IDs are app, brouter, location-search, and map-server. The existing top-level image fields must match components.app. Feeds without a component map retain application-only behavior. Public release versions describe the combination; individual image build tags remain independent. Git revisions are diagnostic only.

A component-only release may reuse the application image. Installed release identity comes from the self-managed component combination; the completion notice uses its component inventory, so updating search alone clears its offer. Registered builds from later releases are never offered a downgrade. Custom unregistered builds remain unknown. Each component build identity has one immutable image/digest binding across all releases.

Optional compatibleBuildIds lists explicitly supported older builds; the target build is always supported. Omit the list when compatibility is unconfirmed. An explicit list excluding a known older build marks that component as requiring an update for the target release. This does not affect application health or disable features. Provider API rollouts must preserve compatibility with supported clients; release discovery is not a service-health check.

Ownership is configured, never guessed from a URL. A remote service can still be self-managed. Compose defaults routing/search to SELF_MANAGED and maps to PROVIDER_MANAGED. For provider-managed routing/search, change the corresponding environment values. For local maps, enable local-maps and set MTL_UPDATES_MAP_SERVER_MANAGEMENT=SELF_MANAGED.

Compose environment variable Default
MTL_UPDATES_BROUTER_MANAGEMENT SELF_MANAGED
MTL_UPDATES_LOCATION_SEARCH_MANAGEMENT SELF_MANAGED
MTL_UPDATES_MAP_SERVER_MANAGEMENT PROVIDER_MANAGED

Allowed values: SELF_MANAGED, PROVIDER_MANAGED, DISABLED, UNKNOWN. Outside Compose, ownership defaults to UNKNOWN. Spring configuration uses mtl.updates.components.<component-id>.management and optional .status-url; otherwise existing component status URLs are used. Environment property names remove component hyphens, for example MTL_UPDATES_COMPONENTS_LOCATIONSEARCH_MANAGEMENT.

Self-managed maps require a reachable status URL: enable local-maps for the Compose service, or configure mtl.updates.components.map-server.status-url for a remote service. An unavailable map service affects its own observation; other components continue checking. Use PROVIDER_MANAGED or DISABLED when that matches the installation; ownership is never inferred from reachability.

Only self-managed, enabled services are probed. Their status response supplies versionInfo.image.version. Requests run in the update worker with a 3-second whole-request deadline and the same size limit as the feed. Provider-managed and unknown services receive no update-discovery requests. Snapshots never wait for network activity. Successful observations refresh on demand at most once per minute; failures retain the last build and back off for 15 minutes. Manual checks can retry after one minute. The browser allows the feed plus three sequential component probes to finish within its 35-second request deadline.

PostgreSQL/PostGIS maintenance remains an operator task, with separate major upgrade instructions. Embedded libraries belong to their image release. Map and routing dataset freshness remains separate from software updates. The checker never reads the Docker socket, installs images, or restarts services.

Network restrictions

Checks run in a separate background worker and never block startup, normal API requests, imports, or navigation. Connection timeout is 3 seconds; the whole request, including a stalled body, is bounded to 12 seconds and 256 KiB. Refused connections, DNS/TLS errors, HTTP failures, invalid feeds, and component probe failures produce a short INFO log; stack traces are DEBUG only. There is no global warning, error dialog, or failed health status. Updates shows a quiet explanation. The last valid result stays cached in memory if a refresh fails. Unknown component IDs and channels are ignored. Invalid releases and their channel pointers are skipped; conflicting build bindings exclude every affected release. Broken feed structure or unsupported schemas still reject the response. Additive changes must retain schemaVersion: 1. A breaking schema needs a new endpoint while the existing URL continues serving schema 1 for older installations. Publication dates are validated by the publisher, independently of the consuming server's date and time zone.

An active browser checks the cached API hourly and on focus/reconnection. The server fetches at most daily, with a 15-minute failure retry gate and a one-minute manual-check gate. Concurrent browsers share the server result. No installed identity, username, or archive data is sent to the feed.

To make no release-feed requests, set MTL_UPDATES_ENABLED=false in the Compose environment and recreate the app container. MTL_UPDATES_CHANNEL defaults to stable; align it with the image channel you run. Development checks are disabled by default, as are demo checks. Offline installations can update manually.

For a private mirror or test feed, set MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL in the Compose environment or .env, then recreate the app container:

MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL=https://updates.example.com/releases/releases.json

docker compose up -d --no-deps --force-recreate app

The default remains https://mtl-explorer.com/releases/releases.json. The URL must serve the same release-feed JSON over HTTP or HTTPS and be reachable from the server container. For a test server on the Mac host, use http://host.docker.internal:18769/releases/releases.json; container localhost refers to the container itself.

Outside Compose, set Spring's mtl.updates.feed-url or the environment variable MTL_UPDATES_FEEDURL. Compose maps the readable MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL name to this Spring environment name. The browser continues to use the server's cached result.

Release publication

  1. Choose the public version and prepare its reviewed release notes. Keep released_on: null until publication.

  2. Commit the application source and build an unused immutable Docker tag with docker-build-deploy.py, or select an existing verified build. Build records identify the image by build ID and digest, independently of the public version.

  3. Publish/promote the image channel intended for users and verify it. Keep the generated image record in the private repository; never invent a digest or reuse a published build tag. For stable, promote the tested build to Docker latest:

    ./docker-build-deploy.py --app-only --tag-latest-only --app-tag BUILD

    Replace BUILD with the unused tag you actually built. The record is in ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/operations/releases/builds/mytraillog-BUILD.json by default. Commit it in the private repository. See container builds for output overrides.

  4. Set the note's actual publication date. Run the normal publisher with the record, for example:

    python ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py v.0.9.0 "MTL Explorer 0.9.0" \
  --image-record ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/operations/releases/builds/mytraillog-BUILD.json \
  --update-channel stable

  5. The publisher checks the immutable image and the corresponding Docker channel (stable → latest) against the record's live registry digest before binding the release in documentation/release-notes/artifacts.json. It regenerates the homepage, notes, archive, and docs/releases/releases.json before copying the mirror. Commit the reviewed source catalog and generated output in the primary repo.

  6. Publish through the existing confirmations, then check the public feed, notes, update guide, and a registered older installation.

Published bindings are immutable. Draft notes, unregistered notes, sync-only, release-only, and GitHub draft/prerelease operations do not create update offers. The public catalog starts empty; no historical image mappings are inferred. The current website tooling uses numeric public release versions. Beta/alpha pointers can select published numeric releases; prerelease note authoring is outside this first implementation. For example, --update-channel beta verifies Docker :beta and advances the beta feed pointer for v.0.9.0. It does not require GitHub's --prerelease flag; that flag intentionally excludes publication from the update feed. Numeric beta/alpha releases appear in the website's regular release list. When creating their GitHub release, the publisher also explicitly passes --latest; the update channel does not isolate them from public release announcements.

Isolated E2E preview

Use an existing development container for Java and a disposable database. Never change production channels or the real public catalog to simulate an update.

python -m documentation.tools.website.prepare_update_preview \
  /Volumes/EXT_HD_1TB/mytraillog/update-preview
python -m http.server 18769 --bind 0.0.0.0 \
  --directory /Volumes/EXT_HD_1TB/mytraillog/update-preview/docs

Set the test server's MTL_IMAGE_VERSION=1.508, enable checks, and point MTL_UPDATES_FEED_URL (Compose) or mtl.updates.feed-url (Spring) to the fixture URL reachable from its container. Verify notice, dismissal/reload, badge, details, skip, and restore on desktop and phone. Restart only that test server with build 1.520: the badge clears and one completion notice appears. Point it to a refused or stalled endpoint and verify login, map interaction, normal API calls, INFO logging, and Updates fallback. For a browser-worker upgrade, serve two distinct production frontend builds at one test origin: wait for Reload, choose Later, confirm work is retained, then reload explicitly. A development Vite server does not register that worker.

Automated coverage: ReleaseFeedClientTest, ReleaseUpdateServiceTest, ReleaseComponentInventoryTest, releaseUpdatesStore.spec.ts, releaseUpdateDetails.spec.ts, test_release_feed.py, and test_release_publication.py. See application verification and component verification.

Publishing a component bundle

Full Docker builds also write mtl-bundle-BUILD.json, named for the application build ID, in the same private release-record directory. App-only builds record only the app. Commit the manifest in the private repository before publication. Use --bundle-record PATH instead of --image-record PATH with ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py, for example:

python ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py v.0.9.0 "MTL Explorer 0.9.0" \
  --bundle-record ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/operations/releases/builds/mtl-bundle-BUILD.json \
  --update-channel stable

The publisher verifies every listed immutable image digest and selected Docker channel before registering the bundle. It never installs it.

For a component-only release, explicitly select the previous tested bundle and replace the changed artifact with its published immutable image:

python -m documentation.tools.website.prepare_release_bundle \
  --base-record /path/to/previous-bundle.json \
  --component location-search=wauwau0977/mytraillog-location-search:BUILD \
  --output ../mtl-explorer-private/docs-my/operations/releases/builds/search-update-bundle.json

Replace BUILD with the actual immutable tag. The helper reads its registry digest and retains unchanged components. Repeat --component for more changes; use --component app=IMAGE:BUILD to retain sidecars after an app-only build. If the base record contains only the app, explicitly add each sidecar to track with another --component argument. Changed artifacts do not inherit old compatibility claims. The helper neither promotes channels nor publishes, and refuses to overwrite an existing record. Test the resulting combination, promote its selected channels, and pass the record to ../mtl-explorer-private/publish-to-github.py --bundle-record with the chosen public version. App-only build records remain app-only unless a base is explicitly selected. Every bundle includes the unchanged application artifact. Existing component build tags cannot be overwritten; full builds reject reused tags for every image they build. Tag-only mode promotes existing artifacts. Keep private Git metadata out of the manifest.

For reproducible deployments, pin Compose overrides to the verified manifest digests. Independent moving latest tags do not establish compatibility. Update only affected services according to release notes; database major upgrades have a separate operator procedure.

To preview a component-only offer with an unchanged server image, add --components to documentation.tools.website.prepare_update_preview. The synthetic catalog offers 0.9.1 to server build 1.508 and search build 2.1; search 2.2 clears it.
